files.signer_sha256: hex of the APK signing certificate

server_sync.auth: client key (laravel_signed_cli), same as other /api/system routes

source_base_urls: builder origins that serve url_prefix (mesh / LAN)
request.upload: fallback: chunked upload when the server cannot reach any source

server_sync.rule: After a local publish the build asks the Laravel server to mirror the app's manifest and files into the server's own <data dir>/<dir_name>/<app>/ with the same idempotent publish rule (sha256 verified before rename, keep_versions). Idempotent: an unchanged manifest is a no-op. Only the platforms listed in platforms are mirrored (the public server needs the installable android app only). The sync is a queued single-flight job (status_endpoint); source_base_urls are tried in order and the first manifest that answers wins.
server_sync.upload_rule: Fallback when no source is reachable from the server: POST upload_endpoint with a signed JSON body {app, file, size, sha256, offset, chunk_b64, chunk_sha256} per chunk (at most upload_chunk_max_bytes raw bytes). The server stages <dir_name>/<app>/<staging_dir>/<file>, answers the next expected offset (an offset mismatch answers 409 with the current offset, so uploads resume), and verifies the whole-file sha256 when the last chunk arrives. Then POST upload_commit_endpoint {app, manifest} publishes the manifest from the staged files with the normal idempotent publish rule.
server_sync.disk_rule: Refuse the sync or upload when free space on the downloads volume minus the bytes still to be fetched would fall below min_free_bytes_after (server disk-full incident 2026-10-08).

app_downloads.public_alias_rule: Each alias path is served by FrankenPHP on every host that serves url_prefix as a rewrite to <dir_name>/<app>/<latest_file with ext public_alias_ext> (Caddy cannot read the manifest), with the .apk Content-Type and Content-Disposition headers; it is a short custom download URL (e.g. https://api.si.12gm.com/wordnew.apk). So latest_file ({app}-latest.apk) must always be the app's newest android release file, falling back to the newest android file when no release exists; a non-release (debug) android publish writes latest_file_non_release instead and only claims latest_file while no release entry exists.

auto_update.mesh_rule: mesh sources are the headscale (*.mesh.*) origins the app already knows: the selected pycore host's mesh origin and the Laravel work-node roster hosts; tried before public_base_urls; first manifest that answers wins
auto_update.channel_rule: the app follows its own build_type; a candidate must have the same application_id and signer_sha256 as the installed app and a higher version_code
auto_update.rule: Android app only. Check manifests, download the APK into app-private cache (resume, sha256 verified), then hand it to the system package installer as an in-place update (same package and signing key keep all app data; never uninstall). The user confirms the install (Android requirement; 'install unknown apps' must be allowed once for the app). Never re-download a file whose sha256 is already cached; delete cached APKs after a successful update.

app_downloads.rule: Downloads live in <core_node data dir>/<dir_name>/<app>/ (never in the repo). A build publishes idempotently: same sha256 as the manifest entry = no-op; otherwise copy to a temp name, rename over the versioned and latest files, then rewrite manifest.json the same way; keep the newest keep_versions per (platform, build_type). FrankenPHP (Windows and Linux Caddyfiles) serves the directory read-only at url_prefix with a file_server (no PHP, no directory listing), manifest.json with Cache-Control no-cache, .apk with Content-Type application/vnd.android.package-archive and Content-Disposition attachment.

paths.linux_www_ntfs_root_rule: linux_ntfs_nested_www_root is a directory and the linux_www_root mount has an FSTYPE in ntfs_fs_types and a SOURCE different from the / mount SOURCE
paths.linux_ntfs_policy: code_and_shared_data: on Linux an NTFS mount (FSTYPE in ntfs_fs_types) holds source code and the data both OSes share (the shared data dir linux_ntfs_nested_www_root/core_node_data_dir_name = D:/www/core_node, and shared files both OSes read; user D26). Never on NTFS: install paths, package caches/stores, build output, compile bases, temp dirs, node_modules/vendor/.venv, Linux-only service state (e.g. database clusters), and no recycle bin (user D25): nothing is sent to a trash on an NTFS mount and per-volume .Trash-<uid> creation is blocked idempotently (development-guides/LINUX_SHELL_RULES.md).
paths.linux_data_dir_selection: an exported CORE_NODE_DATA_DIR wins; otherwise the first applicable candidate that exists or can be created and is writable; path and join name sibling paths keys; home_data_dir_fallback is used without a writability test

drive_layout.purpose: Dual-boot drive layout (user-approved in session core-node-e9; record docs_fix/DESIGN_SHELL_HOSTS.md): tools, caches, venvs and node_modules off NTFS; D: data only Revised by user D27, D28 and D30 (one namespace directory per drive/filesystem: development-guides/DIRECTORY_NAMESPACE_RULES.md).

namespaces.rule: every directory the project creates lives under one namespace per drive/filesystem; no other new top-level dirs; legacy top-level dirs stay until a user-approved migration

program_drive_create.purpose: Step 1 keeps the program drive at min(max_mb, available): it is created in unallocated space of the data drive's disk, else by shrinking the data drive (below min_mb it takes small_ratio of the shrinkable space); later runs extend it into trailing unallocated space, then merge leading unallocated space by copying it into a new partition there (merge_label, old partition relabeled retired_label then removed); when the data drive sits right before that space it is shrunk toward max_mb during a merge, or to start one when the program drive has less than grow_free_below_mb free
program_drive_create.label: programs

drive_layout.program_partuuid_source: detected per machine (the E: NTFS volume PARTUUID), stored in global vars, never committed

downloads_root.purpose: Windows-only installer/package downloads (archives, setup files). Never on D: (shared data only); without E: they stay in legacy_program_dirs.downloads_root

work_root.purpose: Windows-only scratch for unpacking, extracting and building program files. Never on D:; without E: the D:\.tmp temp dir is used

legacy_program_dirs.purpose: Pre-D30 Windows program dirs on D: (user-approved migration 2026-10-03), so D: holds shared data only: D:\.dev_<sys> -> E:\_<sys>_dev, D:\applications -> E:\applications, D:\.tmp\Downloads -> E:\_<sys>_dev\Downloads, D:\.pnpm-store -> <cache_root.windows>\pnpm-store, D:\www\cache\core_node\downloads -> downloads_root, D:\www\cache\pip -> <cache_root.windows>\pip (D:\.tmp itself stays: shared temp). Migration branch only (a fresh install has no old dir): while an old dir still holds program entries, Step 1 (1) copies every entry not yet in manifest_name with PowerShell Copy-Item (in-use files still copy), recreates inner links (broken ones are dropped) and verifies every file; any failure stops here and nothing is deleted; (2) switches: records the verified set in the manifest, rewrites the old and superseded_tool_roots in E: text files, re-roots PATH and every environment variable (WindowsPathFunction.ps1 moveroot), launcher .exe files (relocate_script), shortcuts, scheduled tasks and registry (SystemReferenceRelocation.ps1), runs scoop reset * and records the live dirs (windows_resolved_vars); (3) deletes each D: entry file by file with remove_script (locked files stay until the next run), removes obsolete_staging_suffix leftovers, moves entries matching keep_patterns (models, drafts) to kept_data_root\<target dir name> on D:, and removes the old dir once empty. No link is left at an old path
legacy_program_dirs.work_root_note: work_root is only the value used without E: (and before Step 1 records WORK_DIR); D:\.tmp is shared temp and is never migrated

windows_resolved_vars.purpose: Per-OS var-center keys where Step 1 (SharedCacheEnv.ps1, the only Windows resolver) records the live Windows tool and app dirs; pycore and Laravel read them on Windows instead of re-resolving, and fall back to legacy_program_dirs before the first record

drive_layout.trees_rule: Windows (D28): when the E: program drive qualifies, node_modules/vendor/.venv of each project are junctions from the repo to <trees_root.windows>/<ns>/<dir>; never created on the D: fallback: while E: is absent the code warns and keeps the normal in-repo directories. Linux: ext4 <trees_root.linux> is bind-mounted once onto the single EMPTY mount point trees_mount_linux (under the namespace /www/core_node_compiler) on the NTFS share (mountpoint -q before any write; unmounted it stays empty) so translated junctions resolve to ext4; for a project whose entry is a plain directory (Windows without E:), a per-project runtime bind from <trees_root.linux>/<ns>/<dir> over the in-repo directory is used. Linux makes zero writes and no reparse points on NTFS. The junction translation must be proven on the real dual-boot Linux (ntfs3/ntfs-3g) before it is relied on.

scrcpy_bundle_dir.purpose: Android scrcpy bundle (adb, scrcpy, scrcpy-server) installed by the shell device-tools step: Linux <cache_root.linux>/<dir_name> on ext4 (a Linux-only binary install never goes on NTFS); both OSes export the resolved dir as SCRCPY_HOME (Windows: <tool root>\<dir_name>)

mcp_chrome.service_description: Core Node MCP Chrome watcher and recovery supervisor

ssh_client.purpose: Client-side ssh keepalive for every interactive ssh this repo launches: generated ssh<N> scripts (ssh_command_generator.py) and the claude team launchers (claude_team_common.sh, ClaudeTeamCommon.ps1). ServerAlive* detects a silently cut path (CGNAT rebinding) within interval x count_max seconds; TCPKeepAlive no avoids drops on transient route breaks. Server side: ssh_server_common.sh.

code_sync.purpose: When gitsync is run with the explicit notice flag (never by default) and the push succeeds, the client asks the Laravel server (client key auth, client 'shell') to run one fixed single-flight job: gitsync --skip-notice-laravel, safe migrations, graceful FrankenPHP worker restart only when the pulled commits touch reload_paths (minus reload_excluded_paths; FrankenPHP worker reboot can crash the process, php/frankenphp#2568). The status endpoint reports the phase; wait for it before reading server logs.
code_sync.conflict_ai_prompt: The core_node repository at {repo} has an unresolved git merge conflict from gitsync. {context}Resolve every conflicted file so that all features from both the remote and this machine are kept. Then git add the files, finish the merge with git commit --no-edit, and run the project's gitsync to push.{cleanup}
code_sync.conflict_ai_prompt_cleanup: Then delete {doc} and the first line of {readme} that starts with {marker}.

pipeline.purpose: pycore automatic gitsync pipeline: runs start on a per-machine wall-clock slot (hash of the machine id inside the interval); before running, a pycore takes the LAN turn from every reachable LAN pycore (peer/gitsync/claim; the oldest ticket wins, ties by machine id; the grant expires after claim_ttl_seconds); after the run it releases the turn to every LAN pycore with a compact result (peer/gitsync/release), which feeds their LAN view and, when it pushed commits, schedules their own gitsync after a jittered delay; pushed commits are also written to the agent bus note <note_prefix><machine> with a notice to channel:<channel>. The UI reads ui/gitsync/state with known_revision and refreshes on the gitsync.changed journal topic.

codemart_admin_password.purpose: CodeMart seeded-account password, generated by the deploy ensure step (175 / Step175) on every run after a [Y/n] prompt (default Y; non-interactive = Y), applied to the database at once, saved, printed, viewable any time (user D17)
codemart_admin_password.artisan_apply_scope: every CodeMart account the seeder creates (admin and demo users); hashed with the app hasher; idempotent
codemart_admin_password.seeder_rule: the seeder never hardcodes a password: it reads secret_file, and when the file is missing it generates one with the same length/alphabet, writes it with file_mode and prints it

ai_models.purpose: AI model install level (gvar level_key; installer menu [A]). A model step runs when its level is at or below the selected level in levels order; none installs no model step. Default: default_gpu when an NVIDIA GPU is present, else default_cpu. basic = OCR/TTS only, under basic_download_budget_mb of downloads in total. Keys of levels_by_id are prerequisites.steps ids; extra_steps lists model steps outside that manifest.

prerequisites.purpose: The ONE ordered pycore prerequisite manifest (dependency order). Read by prepare_pycore_prerequisites.sh (Linux), PycorePrerequisitesList.ps1 (Windows) and pyutils/common/prerequisite_steps.py (missing-prerequisite report). linux/windows list the scripts of a step in run order; an empty list means no step exists on that platform. skip_env: variable that skips the step when 1. mode: '' always runs, 'local_ai' opt-in (local_ai.install_env or an explicit include), 'neural' joins the neural TTS batch, 'explicit' needs an include or its own install variable. full: the step accepts --full / -Full. provides: prerequisite names the step satisfies (default: its id).

laravel_rescue.purpose: Linux Laravel rescue plane: a busybox httpd (ports.laravel_rescue_httpd) whose signed CGI (client_key_auth, client shell) only writes <epoch>-<nonce>.<action>.request files into <CORE_NODE_DATA_DIR>/<requests_subpath>; the watcher unit polls every poll_seconds, deletes each file at once and runs its Laravel action. The docroot index page signs the same CGI calls in the browser with CORE_NODE_CLIENT_KEY_1; with keepalive on the watcher restarts the Laravel (ports.laravel_api_backend) and UI (ports.nexus_dash_frontend) units whose port stops listening.

service_manager.purpose: Windows dd.cmd > Service Manager catalog: every service/scheduled task the installers register. kind=service (Windows service) or task (scheduled task); the first existing name wins. dynamic_service_patterns adds matching services discovered at runtime. Linux keeps its registry in scripts/shells/linux/menu_itemshells/service_manager_registry.sh.

book_seed.purpose: Bible corpus seed: an xz tar disguised as .js, extracted by the shell prerequisite step (175_laravel_main_start.sh / FrankenPhpManager.ps1) and only read by Laravel's sys:init.

notebook_defaults.purpose: Defaults of hosted notebook nodes (Colab/Kaggle). notebook_runtime.sh exports assist_default_env=1 unless the caller set it; pyctl/assist/assist_settings.py then treats the listed capabilities as enabled while the user has no stored assist_laravel section (a stored value always wins), so the node assists the Laravel queue (audio lanes, translation) immediately. tts_engines: per platform, the only neural TTS engines installed (in every accelerator mode) and kept in the pinned tts_runtime_plan chains (notebook_runtime.sh, pyutils/tts/runtime_profile.py); a platform without a row installs the engines of the active plan mode.

tts_runtime_plan.purpose: Pinned startup TTS engine chains per capability and mode (pyutils/tts/runtime_profile.py reads them; notebook_runtime.sh installs only the engines of the active mode). Engines outside the plan are never auto-scheduled. The word_batch chain is the single owner of the word-batch engine (Queue Center word audio, Laravel and UI read it here).
